scope: Local native preparation of a signed AS2 MIME entity and single-recipient authenticated CMS envelope

red.observation: The original native command could open an envelope and had no outbound sealing entry point.

independent_fixture_correction.observation: OpenSSL 4.0.3 without its CRLF mode retained the CR from a delimiter on both its own and freightctl MIME. Repeating both with -binary -crlfeol recovered the original signed entity and verified the signature without changing the product wire bytes.

green.environment: macOS ARM, Go 1.27.4, stock OpenSSL 4.0.3, private task-owned files
assertions: Stock OpenSSL decrypted the native AuthEnvelopedData and verified the fixed leaf signer. Its recovered bytes exactly matched the original MIME entity.
The native open path independently recovered the same original entity from the generated envelope. Fresh preparation produced different encrypted bytes.
Wrong signing key, a recipient certificate restricted to signing, and a pre-existing output were refused. The original sealed output was preserved.
The native protected open, signed receipt, and crypto architecture checks passed again.

remaining: Run exact native Linux proof. Implement authority-bound durable storage and HTTP send/receive, safe retry using the same prepared body and message ID, signed receipt creation and persistence, rollover, larger streams and stock AS2 application qualification.
